text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi underscores the important role of the media in the social and economic development of Kenya.
- Opposition parliamentarian Raila Odinga recaptures his seat in a by-election at Langata in Nairobi.
- Attorney-General Amos Wako orders a public inquest into the death of Nairobi University student leader Solomon Muruli.
- Ninety-seven people arrested during the Langata by-election are charged with possession of dangerous weapons.
- A High Court judje rules a directive saying courts should not hear disputes between political parties is not part of the law.
- The government is concerned about drug trafficking through unauthorised landing points along Kenya's south coast.
- The ruling party's candidate for the Langata by-election accuses Raila Odinga of importing voters from other areas.
- A cross-section of leaders send out a water shortage alarm caused by prevailing drought in parts of the country.
- Some pilots at Wilson airport in Nairobi are behind a racket in which hundreds of foreigners fleeing war in neighbouring countries arrive in Kenya. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
